titles: Straying Goats and a Careless Fire
frames: {b} brings {a} before the elders of {town}. {@damage}. There was no malice, only carelessness.
At the gate of {town}, {b} demands that {a} answer for a loss: {@damage}. {a} admits it but pleads that he never meant harm.

options.text: Through careless fencing, {a}'s goats strayed into {b}'s vineyard and stripped the vines
A brush-fire {a} lit to clear thorns spread and consumed {b}'s stacked sheaves of grain
{a} dug a cistern by the road and left it uncovered; {b}'s ox fell in and died
options.ev: ox died in an uncovered pit

hint: The Torah gives a different remedy for each kind of damage: grazing, fire and open pits.

best.label: Repay from the Best of the Offender's Field
best.summary: Compel {a} to pay from the best produce of his own field or vineyard.

fire.label: Full Compensation for the Whole Loss
fire.summary: Order {a} to make complete restitution for everything that was burned.

pit.label: Pay the Animal's Price; Keep the Carcass
pit.summary: Order {a} to pay {b} the value of the dead beast and take the carcass.

stripes.label: Thirty-Nine Stripes Without Payment
stripes.summary: Punish {a}'s carelessness corporally and award nothing to {b}.

split.label: Split the Loss 50/50
split.summary: Divide the loss equally, since nothing was done out of malice.

five.label: Apply the Fivefold Theft Multiplier
five.summary: Treat the negligent loss like a stolen and slaughtered ox.

rules.rationale: Whoever lets livestock graze in another's field must repay from the best of his own field or vineyard (Exod 22:5).

blessing.title: Boundaries Respected
blessing.effect: Farmers keep their animals penned and neighbours keep the peace.

rules.rationale: Whoever starts a fire that spreads must make full restitution for what burned (Exod 22:6).

blessing.title: Fire Kept in Check
blessing.effect: Farmers take care when burning thorns; the harvest is safer.

rules.rationale: The owner of an uncovered pit pays the animal's owner in silver and keeps the carcass (Exod 21:33–34).

blessing.title: Hazards Covered
blessing.effect: People cover their cisterns, and travellers' livestock are safer.

frames: {@history}. This time the beast broke out and {@target}.
At {town}, {o} stands before the elders. {@history}. The ox escaped and {@target}.

options.text: {o}'s ox had twice gored neighbours, the elders formally warned {o} to keep it penned, and {o} left the gate unlatched
{o}'s ox had always been docile and had never hurt anyone
options.ev: ox had no history of goring

hint: Two facts matter: had the owner been warned, and who or what was killed?

clear.label: Stone the Ox; Owner Blameless
clear.summary: Execute the ox without eating its flesh; {o} owes nothing.

liable.label: Stone the Ox; Owner Liable to Death or Ransom
liable.summary: Stone the ox, flesh uneaten, and hold {o} capitally liable unless a court sets a ransom.

thirty.label: Stone the Ox; Pay Thirty Shekels to the Master
thirty.summary: Execute the ox and pay thirty shekels of silver to the servant's master.

split.label: Sell the Live Ox; Divide Price and Carcass
split.summary: Divide the price of the living ox and the dead one's carcass equally.

oxforox.label: Owner Pays Ox for Ox
oxforox.summary: Order {o} to give an ox for the dead one and keep the carcass.

exile.label: Exile Owner to a City of Refuge
exile.summary: Treat the death as accidental manslaughter by the owner.

fine.label: Impose a Fixed 10-Shekel Fine
fine.summary: Treat the incident as ordinary livestock trespass.

meat.label: Stone the Ox & Sell Its Meat
meat.summary: Pay the victim's family from the proceeds of the carcass.

rules.rationale: When an ox kills a servant, the owner pays thirty shekels of silver to the servant's master and the ox is stoned (Exod 21:32), regardless of prior warnings.

blessing.title: Servant's Worth Recognised
blessing.effect: The master is compensated and owners guard dangerous animals.

rules.rationale: If the owner knew the ox was a gorer, he must pay ox for ox and keep the carcass (Exod 21:36).

blessing.title: Warnings Count
blessing.effect: Owners who ignore a known danger bear the full cost.

rules.rationale: If the ox was not a known gorer, the two owners sell the living ox and share the price, and share the dead ox as well (Exod 21:35).

blessing.title: An Even Share
blessing.effect: No one is ruined by an accident that nobody saw coming.

rules.rationale: A known gorer is stoned with its flesh uneaten, and the negligent owner who ignored warnings is liable to death, the one homicide case where a court may set a ransom on the owner's life (Exod 21:28–30).

blessing.title: Warnings Heeded
blessing.effect: Owners learn that ignoring the elders' warning costs a life.

rules.rationale: When a previously harmless ox kills a person, the ox is stoned and its flesh not eaten, but the owner is free of blame (Exod 21:28).

blessing.title: Fault Where It Belongs
blessing.effect: An owner with no warning is not punished for what he could not foresee.

frames: {o} and {k} come before the elders of {town}. {@case} {o} asks who must bear the loss.
Dispute at {town}: {@case} {k} says he owes nothing; {o} says he must pay.

options.text: {k} borrowed {o}'s donkey for a day's journey. The animal fell and died while {o} was away in another village.
{k} borrowed {o}'s donkey, and it died on the road while {o} was walking alongside it.
{k} hired {o}'s ox for a week of ploughing, and it died of a sudden sickness in the field.
{o} left a ewe in {k}'s keeping. Thieves took it from the fold while {k} slept.
{o} left a ewe in {k}'s keeping. A wild beast tore it, and {k} carried the mangled remains to the elders.
options.ev: kept animal torn by beast; remains produced

hint: Liability follows who had control of the animal and whether the loss was beyond the keeper's power.

pay.label: Order Full Restitution to the Owner
pay.summary: {k} must replace the animal or repay its full price.

nopay.label: Release the Keeper from Payment
nopay.summary: Rule that the loss falls on the owner and no restitution is due.

double.label: Order Double Restitution
double.summary: Require {k} to repay twice the animal's value as a penalty.

half.label: Split the Loss Evenly
half.summary: Divide the animal's value equally between owner and keeper.

stripes.label: Flog the Keeper for Carelessness
stripes.summary: Give {k} stripes in place of any payment.

rules.rationale: A borrower who has the animal while the owner is absent must make full restitution (Exod 22:14).

blessing.title: Borrowers Take Care
blessing.effect: Borrowers treat other people's animals as their own.

rules.rationale: If the animal was stolen from the keeper, he must make restitution to its owner (Exod 22:12).

blessing.title: Keepers Stay Alert
blessing.effect: People guard what is entrusted to them.

rules.rationale: If the owner was with the animal, the borrower does not pay (Exod 22:14–15).

blessing.title: Fair Risk
blessing.effect: Borrowers are not ruined by losses the owner witnessed.

rules.rationale: If the animal was hired, 'it came for its hire' (Exod 22:15); the owner has been paid for the risk.

blessing.title: Hire Includes Risk
blessing.effect: Hired work stays affordable because the hire price already covers the risk.

rules.rationale: If a beast tore the animal and the keeper brings the remains as evidence, he does not pay (Exod 22:13).

blessing.title: Evidence Honoured
blessing.effect: Honest keepers are protected when the loss was beyond their control.

titles: A Stray on the Road to {town}
frames: {a} comes to the elders of {town} asking what the law requires of him. {@case}
At {town}, {a} asks the elders what he owes. {@case}

options.text: He found {b}'s ox wandering loose on the road. {b} lives next door and {a} knows exactly whose it is.
He found a strayed ox on the road and has no idea whose it is or where the owner lives.
He saw {b}'s donkey collapsed under its load by the road. {b}, a man {a} dislikes, is struggling to lift it alone.
options.ev: animal fallen; owner is a rival

hint: The Torah has a different duty depending on whether the owner is known and whether the beast is in distress.

return.label: Return It Directly to Its Owner
return.summary: Lead the animal home to {b} without delay.

keep.label: Keep It Safe Until the Owner Asks
keep.summary: Take the animal home, care for it, and restore it whenever the owner comes looking.

help.label: Stop and Help Lift the Beast
help.summary: Join {b} in raising the animal, even though the two are rivals.

salvage.label: Keep the Find as Salvage
salvage.summary: Rule that finding gives {a} ownership of the animal.

ignore.label: Leave It: It Is Not {a}'s Concern
ignore.summary: Rule that {a} owes no duty to strangers or rivals.

sell.label: Sell It and Hold the Silver
sell.summary: Sell the animal and keep the price until the owner appears.

rules.rationale: If you meet a neighbour's straying ox or donkey you must bring it back to him (Exod 23:4; Deut 22:1).

blessing.title: Neighbours Look Out for Each Other
blessing.effect: Strayed animals find their way home.

rules.rationale: If the owner is unknown or far away, the finder keeps the animal at home until the owner comes looking, then restores it (Deut 22:2).

blessing.title: No One Loses by Honesty
blessing.effect: Finders care for the animals in their keeping, and owners recover them.

rules.rationale: You may not hide yourself from a fallen animal on the road; you must help raise it, even if it belongs to an enemy (Deut 22:4; Exod 23:5).

blessing.title: Rivals Reconciled
blessing.effect: Helping a rival's beast breaks down feuds.
